subject: Exec briefing: PrimeLedger latency regression & term exception
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex@primeledger.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production issues after model deploy (urgent)

Karthik,

We pushed the model upgrade you recommended last night (v5.2 + new int8 quant profile). Since the deploy we see P95 latency ~2x baseline and a spike in 5xx errors from our inference calls. A portion of responses are also returning incoherent summaries (several hallucinations in our compliance flow). This is blocking our onboarding milestone—customers are seeing slow/incorrect results.

Attached a snapshot of our dashboard (primeledger_latency_dashboard.png). We need a rollback or a mitigation plan within the next 4 hours. Our CTO is asking for an exec bridge; he's copied. If Redwood can commit to either an immediate fallback to the previous model or a temporary routing to dedicated capacity while you investigate, that would help.

Please confirm ASAP.

- Alex
PrimeLedger, Head of Integrations

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex@primeledger.com>, PrimeLedger CTO <cto@primeledger.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec briefing: PrimeLedger latency regression & term exception

Team — forwarding an urgent customer escalation (PrimeLedger). Key asks from the customer: immediate rollback or routing to dedicated capacity; executive bridge requested.

Immediate actions I want:
- Rishi: quick triage (latency/error signature + whether this is quant-specific) and recommended mitigation (pin old variant / route).
- Marissa: prepare a short customer note and a proposed commerce term (SLA credit + discounted dedicated capacity for 1 week) to calm the CTO.
- Irene: loop legal if we need a term exception; they may ask for contract language.

I attached a short note template and their dashboard. Let's treat this as high priority — we'll organize a 4pm PDT bridge if we have enough info.

Karthik

Attachments: mutual-action-plan_v2.xlsx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Alex Rivera <alex@primeledger.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exec briefing: PrimeLedger latency regression & term exception

Quick triage summary (initial):
- We see a regression correlated to the new quant profile: the int8 kernel path is causing increased memory pressure and higher KV-cache churn for the short-sequence hotpaths used by PrimeLedger (billing and compliance routes). That increases per-request tail latency and causes occasional 504s when requests timeout under backpressure.
- Error-rate spike originates from a retry storm in their client after seeing increased p99; the root is latency, not decode failures.
- The incoherent summaries are tied to a subtle decoding distribution shift in the new model variant — quality delta is small but measurable on their prompt set.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (low-risk, <60 min):
1) Pin PrimeLedger traffic to the previous model variant (v5.1) — this is a config change we can do per-customer.
2) Turn off the new int8 quant profile for their workload; fall back to float16 or the validated quant profile.
3) If traffic remains high, route a subset of traffic to a small dedicated pool (we can spin up 2x cards under dedicated capacity for a week as temporary relief).

I'll prepare a short runbook with commands and rollback steps and post to the incident ticket (SUP-3219). ETA for pinning -> 20–30 minutes once we get approval from the account lead.

- Rishi
Senior Inference Engineer, Redwood

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@primeledger.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exec briefing: PrimeLedger latency regression & term exception

Alex — thanks for flagging and I'm really sorry about the disruption. We own this.

Planned immediate steps:
- Redwood will pin you back to v5.1 and disable the int8 quant profile for your account (Rishi will execute).
- We'll offer 1 week of dedicated capacity at a 50% discount while we stabilize.
- We'll provide an SLA credit for the impacted window (proposal attached in the mutual-action-plan_v2.xlsx).

Irene — please prepare a short term-exception agreement (one-week scope: discounted dedicated capacity + SLA credit), and advise if any contract amendment is necessary. Rishi — please confirm technical ETA and next steps in the SUP ticket once done.

Alex — we've scheduled an exec bridge at 16:00 PDT today to walk through the technical root cause and our remediation plan. If that works for you, I'll send an invite and a 15-minute agenda.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@primeledger.com>, PrimeLedger CTO <cto@primeledger.com>

Subject: Re: Exec briefing: PrimeLedger latency regression & term exception

Alex / PrimeLedger CTO — thank you for joining the bridge earlier. Recap of actions we committed to during the call: 

1) Technical rollback: PrimeLedger traffic pinned to v5.1 and int8 quant disabled (completed at 15:10 PDT). Rishi confirmed p95 returned to within 10% of baseline and error rates decreased.
2) Short-term capacity: Redwood will provide 1 week of dedicated capacity at 50% discount; billing adjustment to follow.
3) SLA remedy: Redwood proposed an SLA credit for the impacted window; Marissa & Irene will circulate the term-exception document for signatures.
4) Postmortem: Rishi will own the postmortem and produce an action plan to harden quant profile validation (target: draft 72 hours).

Attachments: primeledger_exec_notes.pdf (exec call notes) and our mutual action plan (mutual-action-plan_v2.xlsx).

Alex — please reply if the summary misses anything. We'll keep the SUP-3219 ticket updated with timeline and remediation artifacts.

Thanks — we appreciate your patience.

Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
